answer: She will paint this room tomorrow afternoon.

answer: When will they arrive?

answer: She will not come this evening.

answer: When will the new people move into this house?
issues: The new people is understandable but vague and a little unnatural for new staff; lexical constraint prevents replacing it with new staff or new residents. The unfamiliar warehouse setting does not change the grammatical task.

answer: Will he pack his bags tonight?
issues: Keep his bags: changing to the bags weakens ownership; changing to my/your bags changes person. The stage-team context adds little beyond the familiar sentence pattern.

answer: It will snow tonight.

Tonight, it'll snow.
issues: This is a weather prediction, although the other will statements are called arrangements. Will supports both uses, but the task does not itself test the distinction.

answer: When will you repair my car?
issues: My car fixes the speaker as owner; your car or the car would not preserve the specified relation.

answer: Will she have a haircut tomorrow?
issues: The context usefully separates having a haircut from merely making an appointment. Book a haircut would change the action.

answer: He will arrive tomorrow morning.
variants: He'll arrive tomorrow morning.
Tomorrow morning, he will arrive.
Tomorrow morning, he'll arrive.

answer: When will she telephone me?
issues: Telephone me is valid, especially in British English, but somewhat formal compared with call me. Call me is outside the specified lexical bank.

answer: Will we have a holiday tomorrow?
issues: Have a holiday can mean a holiday/vacation period as well as time off. The Chinese context intends taking time off tomorrow; have a day off would be more precise but changes the required phrase.

answer: They will not leave the day after tomorrow in the evening.
variants: They won't leave the day after tomorrow in the evening.
They'll not leave the day after tomorrow in the evening.
The day after tomorrow in the evening, they will not leave.
They will not leave in the evening the day after tomorrow.
They won't leave in the evening the day after tomorrow.
issues: The required long time phrase is clumsy. Keep the negation scoped to leaving on that specified evening; changing it to they will leave later invents a new arrangement.

answer: When will you paint this room?
issues: The context mentions completion for scheduling, but the prompt asks when you will paint, not when you will finish painting. Adding finish changes the specified action.

answer: Will you telephone me tonight?
issues: Will you can sound like a request as well as confirmation; the context establishes confirmation. Telephone is formal but valid, and me must remain the call recipient.

answer: He flew to Paris a week ago.
variants: A week ago, he flew to Paris.
issues: Flew reports completed past travel. Will fly, has flown a week ago, or flew from Paris would not preserve tense or direction.

answer: When did she go to Berlin?
issues: Did requires go, not went. When has she gone is not the ordinary question about one completed past trip.

answer: She will not fly to London tomorrow, but she will fly to Geneva tomorrow.
variants: She won't fly to London tomorrow, but she'll fly to Geneva tomorrow.

Tomorrow, she won't fly to London but will fly to Geneva.
She will not fly to London tomorrow; she will fly to Geneva tomorrow.
issues: The shared tomorrow can be stated once with understood scope over both destinations. Subject ellipsis in but will fly preserves affirmative will; two separate full stops would violate the one-sentence format.

answer: She will return to London the month after next.

The month after next, she'll return to London.

answer: When did you fly to Seoul?

answer: They will not stay in New York next month, but they will stay in Moscow next month.

answer: She will not return to Geneva next year, but she will return to Bombay next year.

answer: He will fly to New York next month.

issues: The framing explicitly cues future despite calling the source a record. Most review novelty here is a change of subject/city/time.

answer: When will we go to Stockholm?
issues: We must include the speaker in the group; they would change person. The new accommodation story and city do not alter the question structure.

answer: I will not fly to Tokyo the day after tomorrow, but I will fly to Paris the day after tomorrow.

answer: It is eight twenty-five.

answer: They went to Berlin two hours ago.

answer: What time will the doctor arrive?

It's quarter past seven.
